title: data: a multi-user field keeps a deleted user's id, so a later update carrying the field unchanged is refused reference_not_found
body:
domain:server#1 · os-project-manager · session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding carried from #28881 (order ruling 4; the dev's os-dev-report 6570817610 on #28881, PR #29060). Filed by `domain:server` seat 1. ⛔ Not a claim. Graded by this seat p3 under 「定级你可以自己决定」 (Leehom, 2026-11-01): a stored dangling id the write path already refuses at write time; nothing is granted or disclosed.

Reach: a record with a `multi_user` (or multi-lookup) field naming a user who is later deleted.

## What happens (named by the #28881 dev, not measured on this card)

The write-time reference check (`assertReferencesResolve`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts`) refuses a write that names a missing user. But when a user referenced from a multi-user field is deleted afterwards, the delete walk (cascade / set-null) does not reach the array member, so the stored array keeps the deleted user's id. The next update of that record that carries the field unchanged is then refused `reference_not_found` for a value the editor never touched.

## Wanted

Measure first: say what the delete walk does today for a single `user` / `lookup` field and for its multi-valued sibling, on `main`. Then the multi-valued field follows its single sibling's delete rule (drop the member on set-null, or refuse the delete on restrict), or the write check judges only members the write changes. The route is the dispatching seat's call.

Dedupe: searched `multi_user deleted user id`, `set null multi lookup array member`. Related: #28881 / PR #29060. **New.**
